newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra says talks with Optus "hugely complex".
newsitem.headline: Telstra says talks with Optus "hugely complex".

text.p: Australian telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp said on Monday that talks with rival Optus Communications about sharing infrastructure were complex and involved a range of scenarios.
"There are many permutations of possibilities, but this is hugely complex," Telstra Multimedia chief executive Gerry Moriarty told reporters in Melbourne.
"I would not speculate on any particular variant of outcomes at this stage."
Telstra and Optus are discussing options to share their optic-fibre cable networks, rolled out in tandem in major capital cities at a combined forecast cost of A$7 billion.
The two carriers are incurring huge losses from the duplicate networks, which carry competing pay-television and communications services.
Moriarty declined to say if or when an agreement could be reached.
Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston, speaking at the launch of Telstra's new broadband Internet access service in Melbourne on Monday, supported the duplicate roll-out.
Acknowledging it would be "nice" to have a single broadband facility, Alston said the two networks had been built upon the principle of competition.
"Competition has been a major driver of innovation," he said.
Telstra is a partner in the Foxtel pay-TV service with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd.
Optus fully owns the Optus Vision cable network following a recent restructuring.
